comparator.sourceNotes: The programme pages (s0, s1, s2) describe the three-year English-taught curriculum in words only (broad year 1, applied project and research year 2, electives, specialisation and a bachelor thesis in year 3) and give no EC; s2 lists the 2026-2027 courses only in a dynamic overview and links PDFs of earlier curricula, and curriculum.maastrichtuniversity.nl was unreachable. The 180-EC reconstruction therefore uses the 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations (s3), whose Overview 2 gives the curriculum of curriculum 2024 in study hours per module (one credit is 28 hours, Article 1.2 and Article 3.5): year 1 has four core modules of 224 hours (8 EC each), Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking modules of 112, 112 and 224 hours (4, 4 and 8 EC) and Professional & Life Skills I of 336 hours (12 EC), together 60 EC; year 2 has Psychological Citizenship (448 hours, 16 EC), Core 5 Mind, Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking III and IV and the Research Project (224 hours, 8 EC each) and Professional & Life Skills II (12 EC), together 60 EC; year 3 has 24 EC of electives, a 24-EC specialisation and Professional & Life Skills III (12 EC), together 60 EC. Brain, Cognition and Behaviour consists of four modules of 168 hours (6 EC each); the Clinical and Transdisciplinary specialisations consist of three modules of 224 hours (8 EC each). The Regulations treat each year as a single 60-EC study unit assessed through a portfolio, so the portfolios carry no separate credits and are not listed as components. Module content for years 1 and 2 (including the second statistics module and the programming and psychometrics modules) comes from the 2025-2026 course catalogue (s4), in which curriculum 2024 years 1 and 2 were already running; the catalogue's year 3 describes the earlier curriculum and is used only for the content of the specialisation module titles. The Regulations and the programme page list no separately credited bachelor thesis module although s1 states that students write a bachelor thesis in year 3; because the three year-3 blocks already total 60 EC, the thesis is treated as embedded in those components and is not invented as an extra component. The Research Project (cmp-13) is therefore the independent-research component to which the optional research element is attached. The second Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking module of year 1 appears twice in the overview under the same title (cmp-06 and cmp-07) and is reproduced as published. The Dutch-language and English-language registrations of the target share this curriculum. A human may want to confirm the thesis placement and the module contents against the current course descriptions.

questionsApplications.label: How can psychology explain, predict and change how people think, feel and behave in order to improve their lives and their mental health?
How can psychological insight help society face climate change and sustainability, migration and inclusion, digital technology, loneliness, polarisation and social justice?

alternatives.concept: UM's Psychology bachelor teaches how people think, feel and behave through core modules on psychological perspectives, brain and cognition, individuals in context, lifespan psychology (with its clinical conditions) and the mind, supported by scientific-inquiry modules on critical thinking, statistics and psychometrics, a programming module and psychodiagnostics, and (in the Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation selected as the neutral route) psychopharmacology and biopsychology, methods of cognitive neuroscience, memory and perception, and action and motivation. This alternative reproduces that core as closely as UCR's catalogue allows: introductory brain-and-behaviour, social, developmental, clinical and health psychology; a cognitive-neuroscience and biology sequence (neurobiology, perception and action, higher-order functions, psycholinguistics, physiology, pharmacology and mechanisms of disease); statistics, research-methods, research-synthesis, data-science, programming and critical-thinking courses; and philosophy of mind and evolution. UCR has no dedicated course in personality psychology, cognitive-neuroscience methods, motivation, psychological test construction or psychotherapy skills, and no supervised psychology research project; these limits are kept visible rather than filled with weakly related courses.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has seven psychology courses (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Social Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Abnormal Psychology, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Medical & Health Psychology and Advanced Research Seminar), eight courses on brain, cognition and the biology of behaviour (Neurobiology, Perception & Action, Higher Order Functions, Psycholinguistics, Pharmacology, Human Physiology, Mechanisms of Disease and Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine), six on research methods, statistics, data science and programming (Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, Introduction to Programming and Calling Bullshit on critical thinking), Philosophy of Mind, The Science of Evolution and Personal & Professional Development. Brain, cognition and behaviour is the largest strand but psychology and methods together make up most of the programme, so the label names the closest match to Psychology, the brain-and-cognition emphasis and the methods and data-science content, and does not present it as UM's full psychology programme.

alternatives.concept: The programme page names climate, migration, digitalisation, loneliness, polarisation and social justice as the societal problems psychologists are increasingly asked to help solve, and the transdisciplinary specialisation shows how psychological findings can help confront them together with neighbouring disciplines and the sustainable development goals (programme-interest rows on climate change and sustainability, migration and inclusion, digital technology, loneliness and social connection, polarisation and social justice). This alternative takes those societal challenges as its organising logic: it keeps a psychology and methods core (introductory, social, developmental, abnormal and health psychology, statistics and research synthesis) and replaces the brain-and-biology sequence with courses on climate change and its communication, social theory and qualitative research, social movements, human rights and law, comparative politics and conflict, persuasion, diversity and leadership, the psychology and ethics of AI and misinformation, and an applied research project on resilience to radicalisation. UCR has no course on the psychology of migration, of loneliness or of sustainable behaviour as such, so these challenges are approached through the neighbouring social-science, law, communication and sustainability courses rather than through dedicated psychology courses.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has nine psychology and research-method courses (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Social Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Abnormal Psychology, Medical & Health Psychology, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Advanced Research Seminar, Research Methods & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods) and fourteen courses on the societal challenges the programme names: climate change and its communication, sociology and social theory, qualitative methods, social movements and justice, law and human rights, comparative politics and peace and conflict, persuasion, leadership and diversity, AI ethics and misinformation, together with Personal & Professional Development. Because the societal courses outnumber the psychology courses, the label names psychology applied to societal challenges and the four challenge areas it actually covers, and does not suggest a full psychology curriculum.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Alternative 1 reproduces the brain, cognition and biology core and its methods and data-science training; Alternative 2 changes the organising question from how brain and mind work to how psychological insight can address the societal challenges the programme names. It therefore drops the foundation-of-life, neurobiology, perception, higher-order cognition, psycholinguistics, physiology, pharmacology, disease-mechanisms, evolution, philosophy-of-mind, psychodiagnostics, programming, data-science and machine-learning courses (14 courses) and adds climate, sociology, law and human-rights, politics and conflict, persuasion, leadership and diversity, qualitative-methods, social-movement, AI-ethics and applied-resilience courses (14 courses). The two programmes share 10 courses (psychology foundations, statistics and critical thinking), so each differs from the other by 14 courses (105 EC), well above the 30 EC floor.

alternatives.concept: The transdisciplinary specialisation shows how applied psychological findings combine with neighbouring disciplines, and the programme page names work and organisational psychology, health psychology and legal psychology as psychological fields and economics, law, political science, engineering and data science as neighbouring disciplines (programme-interest rows on work and organisational psychology, health psychology, legal psychology, psychology and economics, psychology and politics, psychology, engineering and data science, and transdisciplinary psychology). This alternative takes applied, human-centred decision making in work, markets, law and data-driven systems as its organising logic: it keeps a short psychology and methods core and adds behavioural economics and economic theory with econometrics, organisational psychology, leadership and negotiation, consumer psychology, law and politics, and the data-science, machine-learning, programming and AI courses that psychology, engineering and data science combine. UCR has no course in work and organisational psychology beyond Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, none in legal or forensic psychology, and none in engineering, so these fields are approached through the neighbouring economics, management, law, politics and data-science courses.

Against Alternative 1 it drops the foundation-of-life, neurobiology, perception, psycholinguistics, physiology, pharmacology, disease-mechanisms, evolution, philosophy-of-mind, lifespan, abnormal-psychology, psychodiagnostic and critical-thinking courses (13 courses) and adds behavioural and general economics, econometrics, organisational psychology, leadership and negotiation, consumer psychology, law and politics and AI and decision-making courses (13 courses); against Alternative 2 it drops the climate, sociology, social-theory, human-rights, social-movement, qualitative-methods, persuasion, climate-communication, peace-and-conflict, applied-resilience, lifespan, abnormal-psychology and critical-thinking courses (13 courses) and adds the economics, organisation, consumer, criminal-law and data-science courses (13 courses). It shares 11 courses with each of the two other programmes, so every pair differs by 13 courses (97.5 EC), well above the 30 EC floor.

comparatorRouteSelection.route: Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation (year 3, 24 EC)
comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Psychology bachelor (the Dutch- and English-language registrations are merged), so no named route applies, but the 2026-2027 Regulations (s3) and the programme page (s1) offer three specialisations in year 3 of 24 EC each (Brain, Cognition and Behaviour; Clinical Psychology; Transdisciplinary Psychology) and one of them must be instantiated to obtain a single 180-EC pathway. The three specialisations occupy the same 24 EC of the same 60-EC year, the programme describes psychology as a broad field, and nothing in the official sources marks one as more general or more representative of the programme's identity, so the first-listed specialisation in both sources, Brain, Cognition and Behaviour, is used as the neutral tie-break; UCR course fit was not consulted. The 24 EC of year-3 electives is the open elective space of the general programme and is preserved as one open component rather than filled with invented courses.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine and Introduction to Programming open semester 1 and precede every course that requires them: Research Methods & Statistics and Social Psychology (semester 2) precede Statistics & Experimental Methods (semester 3); Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Perception & Action and Abnormal Psychology (semester 4) and Higher Order Functions and Medical & Health Psychology (semester 5); Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes Pharmacology and Human Physiology (semester 3) and Mechanisms of Disease (semester 6). Foundational courses (Neurobiology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Abnormal Psychology) precede the clinical and advanced courses (Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Advanced Research Seminar), and Introduction to Data Science and Machine Learning follow the statistics courses.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three UCR alternatives are defensible. Alternative 1 owns the fourteen generator-eligible rows (each appearing twice, for the Dutch- and English-language registrations) that describe the core of the programme and its Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation (6250 how people think, feel and behave, 6251 explaining and predicting behaviour, 6252 changing behaviour, 6254 the brain and behaviour, 6255 research and experiments, 6256 statistics, 6257 programming, 6264 brain, cognition and behaviour, 6267 perception and attention, 6268 learning and memory, 6269 biopsychology, 6270 psychopharmacology, 6271 cognitive-neuroscience methods and 6272 neuropsychology, each also appearing 40 rows later for the second registration). Alternative 2 follows the societal-challenge direction (rows 6258 to 6263: climate, migration and inclusion, digital technology, loneliness, polarisation and social justice) and Alternative 3 follows the applied transdisciplinary direction (rows 6266 and 6278 to 6283: transdisciplinary psychology, work and organisational, health and legal psychology, economics, politics, and engineering and data science). Alternative 1 shares 10 courses with Alternative 2 and 11 with Alternative 3, and Alternatives 2 and 3 share 11, so every pair differs by 13 to 14 courses (97.5 to 105 EC) and passes the 30 EC / 4-course floor. The clinical-psychology direction (rows 6253 mental health, 6265 clinical psychology, 6273 diagnosing psychological problems, 6274 psychometrics and assessment, 6275 treatment and care needs, 6276 ethical and legal questions in mental healthcare and 6277 therapeutic interviewing, each also appearing 40 rows later) was tested and rejected as not-substantively-distinct: UCR's entire clinical offering (Abnormal Psychology, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Medical & Health Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Pharmacology and Mechanisms of Disease) is already part of Alternative 1, and UCR has no course in psychological test construction, treatment skills, interviewing or mental-health law, so a clinical alternative would differ only by adding ethics, public-health and qualitative-methods courses that do not implement the direction. The search-only outcome rows (6284 to 6289, with the duplicates 6324 to 6329) generated no alternative. No row is inherited across split targets and the programme has no support-only curricular-topic rows.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both give the broad first view of psychology as the study of behaviour and mental processes from biological, individual and social perspectives; Introduction to Brain & Behavior concentrates on the brain, brain injury and the interplay of nature and nurture, while Psychological Perspectives also covers emotion, learning and memory, personality, groups, language and culture and introduces research methods through problem-based learning.

Both teach how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and the social situation, including social cognition, biases and group processes; Individuals in Context adds personality, individual differences, culture and evolved psychology.

Both study human development from before birth to old age, with cognitive, social and emotional development, major theories and individual differences; Lifespan Psychology also covers clinical conditions and their treatment, which UCR addresses in Abnormal Psychology.

Both relate brain structure and function to behaviour; Neurobiology approaches this from the biology of brains (evolution, comparative anatomy, brain regions and rhythms, animal models and laboratory techniques), whereas Brain and Cognition teaches functional neuroanatomy, neuroimaging and brain-stimulation methods and the brain processes of perception, attention, memory, motor control and language.

Both address memory and attention with experimental approaches and the brain structures involved; Higher Order Functions adds emotion, social cognition, consciousness and decision making, whereas Storing Experiences, Predicting Perception also treats perception as prediction.

Both study how the brain guides goal-directed action, Perception & Action through motor control and sensory processing with methods of cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology; the Maastricht module also covers motivation, for which UCR has no direct course.

Explicitly unmatched: Methods of Cognitive Neuroscience teaches the methods for studying brain function, such as neuroimaging data analysis; no UCR course teaches cognitive-neuroscience methods as such (Perception & Action uses them but is matched to Action and Motivation).

Both teach how drugs act on the nervous system and body and how they are used therapeutically; Pharmacology is a general course on the origin, targets, pharmacokinetics and toxicity of drugs, whereas Psychopharmacology and Biopsychology concentrates on psychoactive drugs and the biology of behaviour.

Both address foundational questions about the mind; Philosophy of Mind covers consciousness, the mind-body problem, personal identity and animal and artificial minds, whereas Mind teaches computational modelling of cognition, computational thinking and embodied and extended cognition, which UCR does not teach in this form.

Both address psychodiagnostics, the assessment of individuals with psychological methods and its ethical issues; Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking III pairs this with reliability analysis, psychometrics and factor analysis, which Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies does not teach (UCR covers factor analysis in Statistics & Experimental Methods), whereas the UCR course adds psychotherapy approaches.

Both teach critical thinking about biases, fallacies and misinformation and how to evaluate claims; Calling Bullshit does so through misinformation, pseudoscience and scientific credibility, while Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking I also teaches logic, statistical reasoning and information literacy applied to psychology.

Both teach research methodology and descriptive and inferential statistics (central tendency and spread, association, hypothesis testing and analysis of variance); Research Methods & Statistics adds research design, surveys and operationalization, whereas the Maastricht module develops probability theory and sampling distributions in more depth and trains statistical scripting.

Both teach the statistical analysis of experimental designs with a quantitative or dichotomous outcome (analysis of variance and covariance, regression and logistic regression); Statistics & Experimental Methods adds factor analysis and non-parametric tests, while the Maastricht module also covers chi-square and repeated-measures designs.

Both teach procedural programming and algorithmic problem solving in Python (control flow, subroutines, data structures and debugging); Introduction to Programming also covers object-oriented programming and testing, while the Maastricht module uses assignments from cognitive, biological and clinical psychology and introduces basic neural networks.

Explicitly unmatched: UCR has no supervised group empirical research practical in psychology (research protocol, ethics approval, data collection, report and symposium); the standardized optional independent research element is placed against this component.

Both have students apply psychological research to a real societal problem with partners outside the university; Youth Resilience to Extremism is one research project on radicalisation and well-being for youth leaders and educators, whereas Psychological Citizenship (16 EC) introduces the full breadth of psychological subdisciplines and a stakeholder project on a locally meaningful problem.

Explicitly unmatched: Professional & Life Skills I trains psychology-specific professional skills (a personality diagnostic report, psychological communication, diversity skills, ethics and portfolio reflection); Personal & Professional Development is a general academic-skills course and a shared transferable function is not a sufficiently direct counterpart.

Explicitly unmatched: Professional & Life Skills II develops psychological communication, active listening and interviewing, conflict management and negotiation and coaching skills with a portfolio; no UCR course trains these psychology-specific professional skills.

Explicitly unmatched: Professional & Life Skills III covers student-practitioner wellbeing coaching, regulation and job-application skills with a portfolio; no UCR course trains these psychology-specific professional skills.
Explicitly unmatched: this is 24 EC of open elective space (faculty electives, a minor, courses elsewhere, an exchange or MaRBLe), and no UCR course corresponds to a specific elective.

notes.text: Both programmes include substantial study of psychology, research methods and statistics. The Maastricht University Psychology bachelor additionally includes specialist work in personality and individual differences, cognitive-neuroscience methods, motivation, psychological test construction and psychometrics, psychological communication and professional-skills training, a supervised empirical research practical and a three-year portfolio assessment, together with a 24-EC specialisation. UCR students can instead combine its psychology, cognitive-science, biomedical-science, methods and neighbouring social-science courses, but those specialist components are not offered at the same level of depth.

The Maastricht University Psychology bachelor organizes study around a fixed sequence of problem-based core modules, scientific-inquiry modules and professional-skills modules assessed through a yearly portfolio, with open electives and one specialisation in year 3. At UCR, comparable subjects are distributed across courses in psychology, cognitive science, biomedical science, data science and the social sciences. The UCR programmes therefore cover related territory through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the Maastricht programme course by course.
